title: 2nd Matter The Criterion Of Scientific Consensus

questions.question: In the passage, whose judgments are not accepted as final in a field of knowledge?
questions.answer: People who are not trained within that field, even if they are accomplished in other areas.

questions.question: Why is an expert from one discipline not automatically reliable in a very different discipline?
questions.answer: Because skill in one subject does not give authoritative knowledge in another subject.

questions.question: What example is used to show the difference between expertise and non-expertise?
questions.answer: A highly skilled engineer is compared with even a very modest doctor in medical diagnosis and treatment.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate materialist philosophers when they speak about spiritual realities?
questions.answer: It treats their objections as weak and not worthy of much weight.

questions.question: What makes those philosophers especially unfit to judge spiritual matters?
questions.answer: They are described as absorbed in physical things and limited to what they can sense outwardly.

questions.question: What kind of agreement is said to exist among the People of Truth?
questions.answer: They are said to share a strong unity on sacred, spiritual, and Divine matters.

questions.question: How is Shaykh Gilani presented in the passage?
questions.answer: As a major spiritual authority who advanced greatly in worship and inner knowledge and reached deep certainty in matters of faith.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do the denials of philosophers compare with the testimony of spiritually realized people?
questions.answer: Their denials are portrayed as tiny and overwhelmed beside the much stronger witness of the People of Truth.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing those denials to a small insect’s sound against a storm?
questions.answer: It emphasizes how insignificant those objections are compared with the force of true spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What main principle opens this part of the passage?
questions.answer: A person must belong to a discipline to speak with real authority in it.

questions.question: How does the passage distinguish greatness in general from authority in a specific subject?
questions.answer: It says broad brilliance or fame does not make someone decisive in every area of study.

questions.question: What role does consensus play in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It shows that only qualified people within a field count in forming meaningful scholarly agreement.

questions.question: Why is a physician’s opinion given more weight than an engineer’s in a medical issue?
questions.answer: Because medical knowledge, not engineering skill, is what fits the problem.

questions.question: What limitation is attributed to philosophers focused only on the material world?
questions.answer: Their minds are confined to physical appearances and so they cannot judge unseen realities well.

questions.question: Which kinds of subjects are said to lie beyond such philosophers’ competence?
questions.answer: Sacred truths, spiritual realities, and matters related to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by mentioning a large number of People of Truth?
questions.answer: It suggests that true spiritual knowledge is supported by a broad and weighty body of witnesses.

questions.question: What effect is created by describing philosophers as overwhelmed and confused in tiny details?
questions.answer: It suggests they are so lost in fragments of the physical world that they miss greater truths.

questions.question: What overall conclusion does this section draw about attacks on spiritual truth from materialist thinkers?
questions.answer: Such attacks should not be treated as equal to the testimony of those grounded in spiritual knowledge.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is required before someone’s judgment can be decisive in a technical or intellectual field?
questions.answer: Real standing within that field itself.

questions.question: What does the passage say about outsiders joining the consensus of specialists?
questions.answer: Their opinions do not count as part of that learned agreement.

questions.question: How does the engineer-and-doctor example support the larger argument?
questions.answer: It shows that excellence in one profession does not override even modest expertise in the right profession.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is criticized in this section?
questions.answer: One who is deeply attached to material things and distant from spiritual realities.

questions.question: What happens to such a philosopher’s ability to recognize spiritual light?
questions.answer: It becomes dull and weakened.

questions.question: Why are the denials of that philosopher treated as lacking value?
questions.answer: Because he judges realities beyond his range of perception and training.

questions.question: What is meant by the People of Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: Spiritually reliable believers who have attained deep certainty in truths of faith.

questions.question: In what way is Shaykh Gilani used as evidence?
questions.answer: He is presented as an example of profound spiritual realization and long-tested insight.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage build between saints and philosophers?
questions.answer: The saints are shown as people of deep certainty in Divine truths, while the philosophers are shown as trapped in material concerns.

questions.question: What is the message of the final comparison between thunder and a mosquito-like sound?
questions.answer: True spiritual witness is so powerful that the objections of materialist deniers barely register beside it.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about speaking with authority in science or art?
questions.answer: Authority belongs to those who are genuinely trained and grounded in that science or art.

questions.question: If a person is famous, learned, and accomplished, what still limits his judgment according to the passage?
questions.answer: He still cannot give a final ruling outside his own area of expertise.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring up both science and art instead of only one kind of field?
questions.answer: To make the principle broad and show that specialized knowledge matters across many disciplines.

questions.question: What lesson should a student take from the comparison between engineering and medicine?
questions.answer: Respect the person whose training directly fits the issue being discussed.

questions.question: How does the passage characterize philosophers who focus only on the physical world?
questions.answer: As people whose outlook becomes narrow, coarse, and cut off from higher realities.

questions.question: What forms of reality are said to be mishandled by such philosophers?
questions.answer: Non-material, sacred, and spiritual realities.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress the agreement of many truthful spiritual authorities?
questions.answer: To show that belief in Divine truths is not based on one isolated voice.

questions.question: What gives those spiritual authorities stronger standing than the philosophers in this discussion?
questions.answer: Their long spiritual discipline and their direct realization of truths related to faith.

questions.question: How does the passage use strong imagery at the end?
questions.answer: It uses a dramatic contrast in sound to show how weak philosophical denials are next to powerful spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What is the central message of the whole section?
questions.answer: In matters of faith and spirituality, the judgments of spiritually realized people carry weight, while materialist denials do not.

questions.question: What rule about expertise is stated at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: People outside a discipline cannot speak with full authority about it.

questions.question: Does the passage treat general intelligence as enough for judging every subject?
questions.answer: No; it says subject-specific competence is necessary.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the medical example?
questions.answer: To show that even a low-ranking specialist may be more trustworthy than a famous non-specialist in that subject.

questions.question: Why are some philosophers described as unfit judges of spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because they are occupied with material existence and limited by sensory thinking.

questions.question: What is meant by saying their minds are restricted to what their eyes see?
questions.answer: They rely too heavily on visible, physical evidence and so miss unseen realities.

questions.question: On what issues is there said to be complete harmony among the People of Truth?
questions.answer: On holy, spiritual matters and truths connected to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Why is Shaykh Gilani singled out?
questions.answer: He serves as a clear example of someone who attained very high spiritual certainty.

questions.question: How should the objections of materialist philosophers be weighed against that kind of spiritual testimony?
questions.answer: They should be seen as far weaker and unable to stand on the same level.

questions.question: What feeling is the closing image meant to leave with the reader?
questions.answer: Confidence that truthful spiritual witness outweighs the denials of materialist thinkers.

questions.question: What is the first claim made in this section about discussions in a specialized subject?
questions.answer: Only those inside the field have the right to speak decisively about it.

questions.question: How does the passage define the limits of someone standing outside a discipline?
questions.answer: Such a person may have opinions, but those opinions are not final or binding within that field.

questions.question: What does the passage say about including outsiders in the agreement of scholars?
questions.answer: It says they do not count as part of that expert agreement.

questions.question: Why is an engineer’s opinion on illness not equal to a doctor’s opinion?
questions.answer: Because diagnosing and curing disease belongs to medical expertise, not engineering.

questions.question: What deeper point does that example prepare the reader to accept?
questions.answer: That spiritual questions also require the right kind of qualification.

questions.question: What traits are assigned to philosophers who deny spiritual realities?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as materially absorbed, spiritually distant, and limited in perception.

questions.question: Why are their denials called worthless regarding spiritual questions?
questions.answer: Because they try to judge matters that lie beyond the reach of their method and outlook.

questions.question: How does the passage support the reliability of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: It points to their great number, their agreement, and the depth of their spiritual realization.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning three levels of certainty?
questions.answer: It indicates a very mature and complete form of conviction in the truths of belief.

questions.question: Summing up the whole passage, what comparison is being made between two kinds of testimony?
questions.answer: Experienced spiritual witness is presented as weighty and authoritative, while materialist denial is presented as minor and insignificant.
